title: Ban on fireworks sales approved for 2026
subtitle: Growing Together East planning framework, Vision Zero safety upgrades, official city bird, Arts and Entertainment Reserve and new procedural by-law.
overview: Council voted to amend the Fireworks and Firecrackers By-law to prohibit the sale of fireworks in Kitchener starting in January 2026 {{vote:m4}}. The change also sets start and end times for the three permitted days (Victoria Day, Canada Day and Diwali) and raises fines. Fireworks can still be bought online or outside the city, and use remains allowed on those days.

Council also adopted, as amended, the Growing Together East land use and zoning framework for three Protected Major Transit Station Areas {{vote:m2}}. It approved a zoning and Official Plan change for 288-292 Lawrence Avenue, from industrial to low-rise residential {{vote:m12}}, and approved the Vision Zero 2025 safety improvements, including an all-way stop at Fairfield Avenue and St Leger Street and a pedestrian crossover on East Avenue at Borden Street {{vote:m7}}.

Other decisions included endorsing the Dark Eyed Junco as Kitchener's official bird {{vote:m1}}, creating an Arts and Entertainment Reserve with a $300,000 transfer from the Municipal Accommodation Tax Reserve {{vote:m16}}, and replacing the Procedural By-law {{vote:m6}}. After closed session, Council also authorized a land acquisition and gave direction on an Ontario Land Tribunal matter.

decisions.detail: Council amended the by-law to ban fireworks sales from January 2026, set permitted hours for setting them off, repeal and replace Chapter 739, and approve higher administrative penalties.

Council adopted the Official Plan amendment and zoning by-law amendments for three Protected Major Transit Station Areas, as modified by an addendum report, and forwarded the Official Plan amendment to the Province for approval.
Council approved an Official Plan amendment and zoning by-law amendment changing the property from industrial employment to low-rise residential.
Council directed staff to implement the 2025 safety improvements, including an all-way stop at Fairfield Avenue and St Leger Street and a pedestrian crossover on East Avenue at Borden Street.
Council endorsed the Dark Eyed Junco as Kitchener's Official Bird.
Council established the reserve for tourism-driven programming and transferred $300,000 into it from the Municipal Accommodation Tax Reserve.
Council repealed and replaced Chapter 25 (Procedure) of the Municipal Code.
Council approved terms of reference for the Animal and Dog Designation Appeal Committee and set a $125 appeal fee.

debate: Fireworks vendors and consumers opposed the sales ban. They argued it would push buyers to online, out-of-town and illegal sources, remove point-of-sale safety education and ID checks, and cost local seasonal jobs. Many asked for higher fines, stronger enforcement and mandatory vendor training instead.

Several delegates suggested banning specific products, such as Roman candles, air bombs and skyrockets, which they said are most often misused. Staff said the Municipal Act does not clearly allow regulating individual types of fireworks, so this would need further review.

Delegates in favour cited environmental harm, effects on birds and animals, noise, and safety incidents. Some asked for a full ban and for drone or light shows. A delegate representing Hindu communities said the sales ban could be a first step toward limiting Diwali celebrations. Councillors who supported the ban said it is not a ban on use and that it would encourage advance planning.

Councillors backing the ban pointed to rising complaints, incidents in parks and by-law officers being struck by fireworks. They said enforcement staffing is limited and that education has already been extensive. Staff said Diwali brought the most complaints.

The Mayor and some councillors opposed the ban. They argued it would not stop bad behaviour, would penalize responsible residents and local businesses, and could erode trust if not seen to work. They preferred education, safety and enforcement.
